correctness.rationale: The full binary-law/absence-Laplace equivalence follows by marginalization and inclusion-exclusion. The zero-count bound for at most 2k+1 exponential terms proves sufficiency with 2k distinct positive durations. The 2k-dimensional open parameter family cannot continuously inject into fewer than 2k Laplace values, proving necessity. Binary-weighted durations attain every subset sum; equal durations yield exactly n distinct sums. A concrete complete Prony reconstruction establishes sufficiency constructively. Finite exact tests check examples but are not the general proof; assumptions, zero-intensity atom, labeling and boundary conditions are explicit.

originality.rationale: Comparisons distinguish the sharp all-duration subset-sum identification iff condition from earlier homogeneous occupancy likelihoods, heterogeneous binomial mixtures, general exponential-moment uniqueness, and repeated binary panel models. The theorem is a design-level classification and sharp minimum-visit law, not a claim to invent Prony reconstruction. Inspected accessible full texts did not state this criterion; inaccessible heterogeneous-occupancy primary text and broad mixture theory remain historical-priority risks.

The full 2009 general dynamic-choice mixture identification theorem was not accessible and could contain an implication for this specialized model.
General Prony/moment theory is known; independent priority review should determine whether the binary-exposure subset-sum iff is already explicit in broader experimental-design literature.
An isolated keyword search cannot establish novelty; no independent historical-priority certification was performed.

value.rationale: Site occupancy under imperfect detection is a core ecological survey-design problem. A sharp iff criterion classifies every deterministic positive visit-duration vector, not an arbitrary finite toy slice. The minimal visit count is logarithmic in the number of positive latent detection classes, as opposed to the sharp linear requirement under equal-duration replication. The same total exposure can be maintained by scaling duration proportions, yielding meaningful insight when per-visit mobilization costs matter. This is global structural identification only; no estimator efficiency, field performance or practical robustness is asserted.
